We’ve upgraded our website and membership experience to make it easier to manage your membership, access benefits, update your information, find AAPM education, and stay connected with the Academy. Use this guide as you get familiar with the new site and your Member Compass. Access Member Compass Getting Started: Access Your AAPM Account If you had an AAPM membership account before the transition , your account is available in our new system. Please do not create a new account . Go to the AAPM login page. Enter the email address associated with your AAPM account and select Continue. If your account is recognized, you should see a message that says “We found your account.” Select Set Password . A password setup/reset link will be sent to your email. Open that email and follow the link to create your password. Once your password is set, return to the AAPM login page and log in with your email address and new password. Important: If the system does not recognize your email address, please do not create a second account. You may have a different email address associated with your existing AAPM record. Contact us and we’ll help locate your account. Access AAPM Login Start by entering the email address associated with your existing AAPM account. If your account is recognized, select Set Password to establish your password for the new system. Once your password is set, return to the login page and sign in. Welcome to Your Member Compass Once you’re logged in, you’ll arrive at your Member Compass — your home base for managing your membership and accessing AAPM resources. Profile and contact information Membership information Invoices, payments, and transactions Event registrations AAPM Education Center Pain Medicine Journal Other member benefits and resources Go to Member Compass Member Compass provides quick access to your membership information and frequently used AAPM benefits. Review Your Profile Please take a few minutes to review your profile and make sure your information is complete and accurate. Email and phone number Mailing address Consider adding your photo. To ensure your photo saves, your photo must be 300px x 300px. Organization Credentials and professional information Specialty and areas of interest Training information, if applicable Keeping your profile current helps AAPM better understand and serve our multidisciplinary community and helps ensure you receive information and opportunities relevant to you. Need to change your name or organization? Some profile information may require staff assistance. Use the Contact Us link in your profile or contact AAPM and we’ll be happy to help. Review your profile information and update anything that is missing or has changed. Access AAPM Education AAPM’s online education is available through the AAPM Education Center, powered by Path LMS. Open your Member Compass. Under Popular Member Resources , select Visit Education . You’ll be directed to the AAPM Education Center. Special Member Education Pricing Some membership categories receive additional education discounts. If you’re eligible, your discount information is available directly in Member Compass. Already Purchased a Course? Your existing courses and educational content remain available through the AAPM Education Center. If you have trouble accessing previously purchased education, contact AAPM and we’ll help. Access the Pain Medicine Journal Eligible AAPM members receive online access to Pain Medicine , AAPM’s official journal. Open your Member Compass. Under Popular Member Resources , select Access Journal . You’ll be directed to Oxford Academic. For the best experience, begin from your AAPM Member Compass so your eligible membership can be recognized. Having Trouble Accessing Full-Text Articles? If Oxford Academic is still asking you to purchase content or you cannot access full-text articles, contact us so we can check your membership and journal access. Membership & Renewals Member Compass displays your current membership category and expiration date and, when applicable, allows you to renew, view invoices, make payments, and review transactions. My Membership Category Looks Different. Is That Correct? AAPM recently updated its membership structure to better reflect the different career stages and professionals represented within our multidisciplinary community. If you believe your membership category is incorrect, please do not create another account or submit a new application. Contact AAPM and we’ll review your record. Students, Residents & Fellows If you’re currently in medical school, residency, or fellowship, please review your training information, including your current program, PGY level, anticipated completion year, and other applicable professional information. Frequently Asked Questions Do I need to create a new AAPM account? No. If you previously had an AAPM account or membership, your record has already been moved to the new system. Begin by entering the email address associated with your existing account on the login page. What if the system does not recognize my email? Please do not create another account. Contact AAPM and we’ll help locate your existing record. I requested a password email but didn’t receive it. What should I do? Check your spam or junk folder and confirm you’re using the email address associated with your AAPM account. If it still doesn’t arrive, contact us. Why can’t I renew yet? Renewal availability is based on your membership expiration date. Contact AAPM if you have questions about when your membership is eligible for renewal. Where can I find my education discount? Eligible membership categories can find their education discount information in Member Compass. How do I access Pain Medicine ? Access the journal through the Access Journal link in Member Compass so your eligible membership can be recognized. Some of my profile information is incorrect. What should I do? Update what you can directly through Member Compass. If a field cannot be edited, contact AAPM and we’ll help. Need Help? If you have questions about logging in, your membership, profile, education access, Pain Medicine , or anything else in Member Compass, please reach out. We appreciate your patience as we continue putting the finishing touches on the new AAPM experience. Samuel Ko - Looking Beyond the Crisis in Pain Care This month, AAPM is proud to spotlight H. Samuel Ko, MD, MBA, a board-certified emergency medicine physician, educator, and clinician whose career has evolved around a fundamental question: What happens to patients when the immediate crisis is over, but their pain remains? Dr. Ko is the founder and medical director of Reset Ketamine in Palm Springs, California, where he works with patients experiencing treatment-resistant depression, PTSD, and chronic neuropathic pain. His approach reflects lessons learned throughout his career caring for patients with complex conditions who have not found adequate relief through conventional treatments. For Dr. Ko, the transition from emergency medicine into caring for patients with chronic pain grew from seeing firsthand the limitations of treating only the immediate problem. "Emergency medicine taught me to stabilize a crisis. But I kept thinking about the patients whose pain didn't resolve once the crisis passed. I spent eight years running a clinic focused on those patients, and what I learned is that chronic pain is complex and requires a multimodal approach. This is what makes the work both hard and worth doing. To the health care system it may be one case, but to that patient it's their life back." Dr. Ko earned his Bachelor of Science from Seattle University and his MD/MBA from the University of Rochester School of Medicine. He completed his emergency medicine residency at Loma Linda University Medical Center, where he developed a patient-centered approach that considers not only the biological aspects of illness, but also the psychological and social factors that can influence healing. Following residency, Dr. Ko served as an attending emergency physician, assistant professor of emergency medicine at a Level I trauma center, and assistant medical director. His experiences in emergency medicine ultimately sparked a deeper interest in ketamine and other neuromodulatory approaches for patients living with severe, refractory symptoms. His clinical experience also includes point-of-care ultrasound and stellate ganglion block procedures. Education has become another important part of his work. Dr. Ko co-created Ketamine StartUp, an educational program designed to help clinicians better understand evidence-based ketamine infusion therapy, and has consulted on the development of more than 20 ketamine clinics across the United States. Dr. Ko is also bringing his experience and perspective to AAPM, recently joining the AAPM Finance Committee. His involvement reflects the multidisciplinary expertise that strengthens the Academy and its work to advance the field of pain medicine. Throughout his career, Dr. Ko has remained focused on the individual behind the diagnosis. His belief that complex pain requires a comprehensive approach, and that successful treatment can mean helping someone regain their life, reflects the patient-centered spirit at the heart of AAPM. We are honored to feature Dr. H. Samuel Ko as September's Member Focus and welcome his continued involvement with the Academy. Understanding the reimbursement model shift if one thing. Knowing whether your practice is ready for it is another. As the transition to value-based care looms closer, pain clinicians and practices are facing important decisions about how to establish effective processes to comply with the Ambulatory Specialty Model (ASM). What will Value-Based Care Reimbursement mean for patient care, clinical workflows, practice operations, and the future of pain care? In the final session of AAPM's The Big Shift educational series, join Dr. Kayode Williams, Dr. KiKe Oduba, and Dr. Marie Hanna for an interactive fireside chat focused on those questions, and on what practices can do now to prepare for what comes next. Building on the concepts and practical strategies explored during our first two webinars, our conversation on September 22 nd will examine the clinical and operational considerations that can help practices assess where they are today and identify areas that may require attention as the value-based care environment evolves. Register Today What You'll Explore Hear what the experts are watching now as ASM implementation approaches and what pain clinicians should have on their radar. Identify where your practice may be less prepared than you think, including potential blind spots that may affect success under the model. Get a first look at a new practice-readiness tool designed to help practices assess their current state and identify areas that may need attention. Separate what matters now from what can wait, so you can focus your time and resources on the most meaningful steps toward readiness. Explore the questions that remain unanswered and what uncertainty around the model means for practice planning. Hear how experts are thinking about real-world implementation, including balance between patient care, administrative burden, outcomes measurement, and financial sustainability. Bring your own questions to the conversation and hear expert perspectives on the issues affecting your practice. Leave with a clearer sense of what comes next, not just what ASM requires, but what your practice can begin prioritizing now. A First Look at a New Practice-Readiness Tool Attendees will also get a first look a a new practice-readiness tool in development with the support and integrity you expect from AAPM. The practice management tool is designed to help practices think more systematically about preparation and be prepared for the upcoming changes they may face, and the ultimate impact on your practice's business model. Rather than approaching the transition as a single operational change, the discussion will explore how practices can begin connecting the pieces that will help them move from clinical care and outcomes measurement to workflows, documentation, data, and coordination. Bring Your Ambulatory Specialty Model Questions for Our Expert Panel This final session is designed to be a conversation. Expert panelists will respond to questions from attendees and discuss the practical realities of preparing for the ASM. We recommend reviewing the preceding two webinars available on demand to inspire your questions in preparation for the September 22 nd ASM Ask the Experts session. Webinar 1 Webinar 2 Whether you have followed The Big Shift from the beginning or are joining the conversation for the first time, the fireside chat is an opportunity to ask questions, assess where your practice stands, and begin preparing for what comes next. Join us September 22 for The Big Shift: Ask the Experts - Navigating the Ambulatory Specialty Model. headings: Welcome to the New AAPM Website!
content: Skip to content ️ Pardon Our Dust! We’re putting the finishing touches on our new website. Thank you for your patience as we get everything settled. Welcome to the New AAPM Website! We’ve refreshed our website to make it easier to manage your membership and access AAPM resources. Existing users will need to reset their password before logging in for the first time. Click Login at the top of the page. Enter the email address associated with your AAPM account . Follow the prompts to reset your password . Once logged in, visit My Profile to review your information and access your member resources. Need help? Contact info@painmed.org . ACKNOWLEDGE in your cart View Cart Cart Join Login PainConnect Journal Donate Contact About About AAPM Leadership Foundation AAPM Corporate Relations Council AAPM Policies International Community Advocacy What Is Pain Medicine? Staff Membership Member Types Benefits of Membership Get Involved AAPM Resident Ambassadors Program Committees & Task Forces Shared Interest Groups AAPM Awards Pain Fellowship Excellence Award Education Education & Events PainConnect Innovation Courses Behavioral Medicine of Pain Certificate Course Pain Perspectives: Understanding and Managing Pain Across Specialties Pain Rounds Value Based Care in Pain Medicine Publications Pain Medicine Journal Pain Matters Podcast Weekly News Brief Voices in Pain Medicine Blog Research Research & Guidelines Clinical Guidelines Neuormodulation and Neurocomputer Interfaces for Pain & Functional Recovery Sacroiliac Joint Complex Pain Guideline Topical Analgesics for Neuropathic Pain Your Career Job Board Contact Join Login September 2026 President's Message Date posted September 8, 2026 in 2026 , President's Message , AAPM September 2026 President’s Message Dear Colleagues and Friends, In my July message, I reminded you that the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) will implement the Ambulatory Specialty Model (ASM) , a program that requires Value-based reimbursement for specialty care, on January 1, 2027. Value-based care represents more than a change in how health care is financed or measured. It is an opportunity to reaffirm what matters most in pain medicine: i mproving meaningful outcomes for our patients, restoring function and quality of life, and delivering thoughtful, evidence-based, sustainable care. We created our Value-Based Care Educational Series to help AAPM members navigate this evolving landscape with confidence. I encourage you to watch our first two webinars , The Big Shift: Value-Based Care and What It Means for Pain Management , and From Understanding to Action . Together, these sessions provide a foundation for understanding value-based care, the CMS Ambulatory Specialty Model, and the practical steps clinicians and practices can take to prepare for what lies ahead. This conversation is only beginning. Join us on September 22 for our upcoming fireside chat, where we will bring together expert perspectives to look beyond the changes ahead and consider how we can collectively shape the road ahead. We will also share practical tools and resources to help you translate these concepts into action within your own practice. Together, we can help shape a future in which value-based care is not simply a change in the health care system, but an opportunity to advance better pain care for our patients, support the clinicians who provide it, and build a more sustainable health care system for all. As an Academy, we have an opportunity—and a responsibility—to lead with vision , remain grounded in evidence, and advocate for a health care system that recognizes the complexity of pain while rewarding care that truly makes a difference. AAPM Strategic Plan Update Over the past several months, AAPM leaders have been developing a North Star Strategy to guide the Academy’s priorities, programming, and investments through 2029. At its center is a clear commitment: to strengthen AAPM as the nationally recognized home and credible voice for Pain Medicine, deliver greater professional value across every career stage, and build the financial strength needed to sustain that work. For you, this will mean more relevant education and career resources, practical evidence-based guidance, stronger advocacy, and meaningful opportunities to connect and contribute. We look forward to sharing more about the strategy and how it will help AAPM better serve you while advancing the specialty in the months ahead. Big Things Are Happening at AAPM Our first step in implementing the North Star Strategy was to implement our New AAPM Website and Membership Model . Listen now for an update from AAPM CEO Sharon Kneebone and me. PainConnect 2027 Call for Abstracts is Open AAPM’s PainConnect 2027 Call for Poster Abstracts is now open through November 11, 2026. I encourage you to submit your research and share the opportunity with your residents, fellows, and peers. The top six non-commercial abstract submissions will be invited to present from the podium at PainConnect 2027 and have their manuscript published in a special Pain Medicine Journal issue.
